grand_strategy.reading:
Portugal runs the strategy of a small Atlantic state that makes itself useful to
every large power around it and commits to none beyond what the treaties force.
Its anchors are three - the EU (money and a Portuguese chair of the European
Council), NATO and the United States (Lajes), and the Lusophone world (Brazil,
Angola, the CPLP) - and its method is conditionality: base access on conditions,
Palestine recognised only with a group, the F-35 kept open, Chinese capital welcomed
but not endorsed. This works while the anchors do not collide. In 2026 they began to:
the Iran war put Lajes between Washington and the Spanish line, the F-16 replacement
asks it to choose between Lockheed and a European hedge it cannot yet pay for, and
the CPLP is splitting over Equatorial Guinea. At home the cost shows in a minority
government, a president of the other party who speaks more sharply than the foreign
minister, and Chega, which polls first on the one issue (immigration) where the
Lusophone strategy and the electorate pull apart. Expect Lisbon to stay the quietest
reliable ally until Washington asks for something it cannot dress in conditions.
